references.notes: Boxes like these \[i.e. boxes holding unnumbered fragments of the K type\] must have been the source of many fragments included by L. W. King in the first Supplement to the Kouyunjik Catalogue, in addition to those from new excavations of 1904-1905 and a few obtained in other ways. His fragments had previously been considered “of too small an importance to justify their inclusion in the numbered collection of tablets” (King 1914: xv). They number K14231-K16794 which is a respectable quantity. While all those chosen by King were then assigned K numbers, he noted where they had belonged to groups such as Rm 2 and 81-2-4, helpful information since there is slightly better information about the provenance of these later groups.
